claims.text: For \((r,n-r,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\), with \(B=(6,6)\), the corrected truncated LR presentation has \(F\)-rank \(27\), \(106\) Pieri rows, and \(281\) LR rows. Both rational quotient-rank computations give \(2\). A selected Pieri sublattice has free columns \(e_{(1)},e_{(2)}\), global unimodular minor \(-1\), and contains every LR row integrally (`LR_rows_not_in_selected_Pieri_lattice = 0`). Its degree-block certificates \((\text{rows};\text{columns};\det)\) are \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} 2&(1;1)&11&1\\ 3&(1;11),(1;2)&21,3&1\\ 4&(1;21),(1;3),(2;11)&22,31,4&-1\\ 5&(1;22),(1;31),(1;4)&32,41,5&1\\ 6&(1;32),(1;41),(1;5),(2;22)&33,42,51,6&1\\ 7&(1;33),(1;42),(1;51)&43,52,61&1\\ 8&(1;43),(1;52),(1;61)&44,53,62&1\\ 9&(1;44),(1;53)&54,63&1\\ 10&(1;54),(1;63)&55,64&1\\ 11&(1;55)&65&1\\ 12&(1;65)&66&1 \end{array} \] Here \((\lambda;\mu)\) denotes the row for \(s_\lambda s_\mu\), and strings denote partitions. [artifact 27afdb63404a159fb655ddde4867d0e60d06159e2e64e4f8523604222057256a]

In both cases, the LR relation lattice equals the selected Pieri lattice: selected Pieri rows are LR rows, while the exact containment test gives the reverse inclusion. The unimodular block minor makes this lattice a graph over all columns except \(e_{(1)},e_{(2)}\). Therefore \[ J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z e_{(1)}\oplus\mathbb Z e_{(2)}\cong\mathbb Z^2. \] Equivalently, the Smith forms are \(\operatorname{diag}(1^{25},0^2)\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(1^{18},0^2)\), respectively.

Here \(a=b=1\), so the two prescribed families are \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}\) and \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}\). The first maps to the displayed basis of the quotient; the degree-\(2\) Pieri relation is \(e_{(2)}+e_{(1,1)}=0\), so the second does also. Hence neither family admits deletion while still generating \(J_v\).
